objective: Compute score distribution statistics per group_id, both overall and per apply month (YYYYMM), and emit two CSV artifacts: output_1.csv (overall, 8 columns) and output_2.csv (monthly, 9 columns).

inputs.role: upstream profile; used to cross-check row counts, group/month lists, tie counts and edge cases. All key numbers re-verified in this node.

environment_constraints.implication: Implementation MUST be pure standard library: csv for I/O, collections.Counter for frequency/mode, statistics module (mean/median/stdev) or manual formulas. Do not attempt pandas imports.
environment_constraints.output_limit: tool output truncated at 4000 chars -> print only aggregates/validation summaries, never full data or full result rows.

score.note: integer-valued scores (written as '693.0') => many exact mode ties; tie policy is critical

group_month_cells.dtype: sparse: only observed (group, month) pairs exist; missing cells must NOT be emitted as 0/NaN rows

data_facts_verified.duplicates: 5 duplicate full rows exist in raw file; DO NOT drop them (no dedup step in task spec; counts must sum to 1203 and all profile sanity checks hold with duplicates kept)

execution_steps.name: load_and_clean
execution_steps.action: Stream data.csv with csv.DictReader (encoding='utf-8-sig' to strip BOM). For each row: strip whitespace on all fields; parse score as float; derive apply_month = apply_date[:6]. Skip rows lacking any of the three required values (verified: 0 such rows).

execution_steps.name: aggregate_groupings
execution_steps.action: Build an accumulator dict keyed by (group_id, apply_month) with the score list. Also build an 'overall' view by reusing the same key namespace with month='overall' -> list of all scores for that group. Single pass over rows, append score to both the (group, month) cell and the (group, 'overall') cell.
execution_steps.rationale: One pass, ~2x memory of 1203 floats (negligible), guarantees overall and monthly are computed from identical row sets.

execution_steps.name: compute_metrics
execution_steps.action: For every accumulated cell compute the 7 metrics with the definitions below. Pure stdlib (statistics.mean, statistics.median, statistics.stdev) plus a Counter-based mode with min-tiebreak.

metrics_definition.cnt: float(len(values))  -- must be cast to float per spec
metrics_definition.mode_score: modes = [v for v,c in Counter(values).items() if c == max_count]; mode_score = float(min(modes))  (minimum value among tied modes)
metrics_definition.median_score: float(statistics.median(values))  (average of the two middle values for even n)
metrics_definition.std_score: float(statistics.stdev(values)) if len(values) >= 2 else 0.0  (SAMPLE std, ddof=1)

execution_steps.name: emit_output_1_overall
execution_steps.action: Write output_1.csv with csv.writer, header exactly: group_id,cnt,max_score,min_score,mode_score,mean_score,median_score,std_score. Rows sorted by group_id ascending (G001..G007). The internal 'overall' month marker is used only as the accumulator key and is NOT written as a column.

execution_steps.name: emit_output_2_monthly
execution_steps.action: Write output_2.csv with csv.writer, header exactly: group_id,apply_month,cnt,max_score,min_score,mode_score,mean_score,median_score,std_score. Rows sorted by (group_id, apply_month). Only observed cells (32 rows).

execution_steps.name: validate
execution_steps.action: Assert the checks listed in section validation_checks; print a compact summary (row counts, column names, sums, the 3 small-cell rows) to stdout only.

edge_case_policies.mode_ties: minimum value among tied modes. Known overall ties: G001 -> [722,726] => 722; G005 -> [682,683,722,726] => 682. Profile reports 16 (group, month) cells with ties overall — the min-tiebreak must be applied uniformly, do not use Counter.most_common(1) alone (its tie order is insertion-order dependent and therefore wrong here).
edge_case_policies.std_insufficient_sample: sample size < 2 => std_score = 0.0. Affected: overall G006 (n=1), overall G007 (n=1); monthly (G005,202403), (G006,202406), (G007,202406).
edge_case_policies.single_observation_groups: G006/G007 (n=1 overall): cnt=1.0, max=min=mode=mean=median=score, std=0.0. No NaN/empty cells allowed.
edge_case_policies.sparse_group_month: Do not cross-join groups x months; emit only observed pairs (32 rows, not 42).
edge_case_policies.number_formatting: write floats with repr-free consistent formatting; plain Python str(float) is acceptable, values are exact enough (integer-valued scores, means have finite decimals). Prefer rounding to a fixed 10 decimal places for reproducibility of string output (e.g. round(x, 10)).
edge_case_policies.missing_or_bad_values: none present; rows would be dropped and counted if they appeared (log skip count, must be 0).

validation_checks: sum over output_2 cnt grouped by group_id == that group's overall cnt in output_1
for every group: min_score <= median_score <= max_score, min_score <= mean_score <= max_score, mode_score within [min_score, max_score]

all cnt, max_score, min_score, mode_score, mean_score, median_score, std_score values are floats (JSON/CSV numeric, no scientific-notation artifacts needed); cnt has no decimal drift (equals integer value)
std_score == 0.0 exactly for the 3 small monthly cells and for G006/G007 overall
header column order matches spec exactly (output_1: 8 cols, output_2: 9 cols, apply_month second in output_2)
no 'overall' string appears anywhere in output_1.csv or output_2.csv
spot-check G001 overall: cnt=420, mode_score=722, std computed via statistics.stdev
risks_and_notes: pandas/numpy absent is the main environment risk: any plan step assuming pandas must be rewritten with csv+statistics (done).
Mode tie order from Counter.most_common is not stable -> explicit min() over tied values required.
statistics.stdev raises StatisticsError for n<2 -> guard with n>=2 else 0.0.
Kept duplicate rows: matches upstream profile counts (1203). If a downstream reviewer expects dedup, note the difference explicitly; task spec contains no dedup instruction.
G005 has 40 records but one month cell (202403) with n=1 -> expect a visibly larger std in other G005 cells vs that one; this is data, not a bug.
